title: Studi Kandungan Fitokimia Ekstrak Etanol Daun Gambir Sebagai Anti Diabetes
author: Viena,Vera
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Prepare dry simplisia
steps.instruction: Collect fresh gambir (Uncaria gambir) leaves, air‑dry them until moisture is low (reported powder moisture ≈ 3.017 %), then grind the dried leaves to a fine powder to obtain the dry simplisia.

steps.title: Ethanol maceration extraction
steps.instruction: Macerate the dry simplisia in ethanol for two successive 24 h periods, screening (filtering) the mixture every 24 h, then evaporate the ethanol to obtain the dry ethanol extract (reported yield ≈ 2.47 g per g dry weight).

substeps.instruction: Add a measured amount of ethanol to the powdered leaves in a suitable container.
Stir and let stand for 24 h (first maceration).
Screen (filter) the mixture and collect the filtrate.
Add fresh ethanol to the residue and macerate for a second 24 h.
Screen again and combine the filtrates.
Evaporate the combined ethanol under reduced pressure or a rotary evaporator until a dry extract is obtained.

steps.title: Determine phytochemical contents
steps.instruction: Analyse the dry ethanol extract for total phenolic, total flavonoid and tannin contents (reported values: Total Phenolic 71, 80 %; Total Flavonoid 32, 06 %; Tannin 58.39 %).

substeps.instruction: Prepare standard curves for phenolics, flavonoids and tannins using appropriate reagents (e.g., Folin‑Ciocalteu for phenolics, aluminium chloride for flavonoids, etc.).
Dissolve a known amount of the dry extract in solvent to the required concentration.
Perform each assay according to the chosen protocol and measure absorbance.
Calculate the percentages using the standard curves.

steps.title: GC‑MS chemical profiling
steps.instruction: Inject the ethanol extract into a gas‑chromatography‑mass‑spectrometer to identify and quantify the chemical components.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve a measured amount of the dry extract in a suitable GC‑compatible solvent (e.g., methanol).
Filter the solution through a 0.22 µm syringe filter.
Inject the filtered sample into the GC‑MS under the instrument’s standard conditions.
Acquire the chromatogram and mass spectra, then interpret the data to list the identified compounds.

steps.title: Alpha‑amylase inhibition assay (optional)
steps.instruction: Test the ethanol extract at a concentration of 1000 ppm for inhibition of α‑amylase activity (reported inhibition ≈ 88.22 %).

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 1000 ppm solution of the dry extract in assay buffer.
Incubate the solution with α‑amylase under the assay conditions.
Measure the enzymatic activity and calculate percent inhibition.
